messages:
inc_bot: :rotating_light: Pager: high KV eviction rate detected on cluster rdx-prod-us-west-2. Affected service: rope-serving. Auto-incident created.
samir: seeing the bot — looking at metrics now. which model traffic?
maria: lots of long-context/NTK requests spiking. prefix cache size grew ~4x in last 10m, eviction storms on several nodes.
devon: users hitting 502/504s? I see increased 5xx from gateway (latency > 2s on first token).
samir: confirmed. broad increase in continuous-batching queue size too. looks like prefetch window blowup interacting with sliding-window KV entries.
maria: hypothesis: a recent rollout that changed default prefetch window + NTK sampling caused more unique KV keys per request, leading to high memory churn and eviction.
devon: logs from node-03: `kv_evictions=124k` in 5m, OOM pressure flagged but GC kept it alive. also `batch_fill_time` spiked.
samir: i'm going to open the quick mitigation runbook. short-term: reduce continuous batch max tokens, disable aggressive prefetch, and set sliding_window=false on the hot fleet.
maria: +1. which flag do we push?
samir: let's do a rolling config change via runtime flags:
samir: ```
# runtime overrides (prod-hot)
continuous_batch.max_tokens=128
continuous_batch.max_requests=8
prefetch.window_size=4
rope.sliding_window.enabled=false
# fallback model variant routing to smaller KV-friendly model
routing.fallback_variant=shortctx-v2
```
devon: pushing to prod-hot canary now for 3 nodes, will monitor.
ops-bot: Deploy started: runtime-flags/2026-03-15T10:04Z to nodes node-01,node-02,node-03. CI checks passed.
maria: dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.example.com/d/kv/rope-kv?orgId=1&from=now-30m — watching eviction rate and batch latency.
samir: after canary looks ok, we'll roll to remaining hot fleet and trigger autoscale to reduce pressure. also notify support for customer impact.
devon: canary metrics look better after 2m: evictions down ~80%, p50 first-token latency down 450ms. no new 5xx in canary.
julie: tagging support: @support-team some customers saw increased error rates between 09:55-10:05 PST. informing them of mitigation steps.
maria: rolling to rest of hot fleet. starting sequential restarts (no full restarts, just reload flags) to avoid cold KV rebuild.
inc_bot: Note: automatic alert threshold cleared for nodes node-01..node-03.
samir: still seeing one noisy machine node-07, evictions high. isolating and cordoning it from load balancer.
devon: cordon + drain started on node-07. moving traffic away.
maria: after traffic shift, node-07 eviction tail drains, CPU stable. good.
samir: we also applied a temporary routing rule to prefer shortctx variants for requests with estimated NTK > 32. that should reduce unique KV cardinality.
devon: quick note for postmortem: root cause likely interaction of two changes deployed in last 24h — prefetch window increase (prefetch.window_size default 16) and new NTK-based sampling that increases tokenized prefixes. together they multiplied KV key cardinality.
julie: customer impact summary in #support: 12 customers affected (API errors, elevated latency). SLA violations: ~3 customers hit minor SLO breach for 5m.
samir: action items: 1) revert the prefetch default to 6 temporarily (samir) 2) add safety cap on prefetched KV cardinality and rate-limit NTK sampling (maria) 3) postmortem and improved canary for flag changes (devon) 4) customer comms draft (julie).
maria: implementing safety cap: `prefetch.max_total_keys=50000` and `ntk.sampling.rate_limit=0.2` — will push as non-disruptive flag.
devon: pushed cap to remaining nodes. monitoring.
julie: sending initial customer note now, include status, mitigation, ETA for followup.
samir: can we add a telemetry alert: if KV unique keys growth > 2x in 5m trigger prefetch auto-throttle?
maria: yes, I'll add that alert and tie to an automated soft-throttle for prefetch.
inc_bot: Incident update: mitigation applied, partial rollback and safety caps in place, ongoing monitoring. Incident severity: Sev3 -> monitoring.
devon: timeline note: root cause deployment at 2026-03-15T09:40Z, regression detected 09:55Z, mitigation complete 10:08Z.
samir: thanks all. follow-ups: postmortem owner devon + maria, customer comms owner julie. low-latency follow-up meeting in 30m. :thumbsup:
julie: will add to incidents calendar and create postmortem doc link: https://wiki.redwood.example.com/incidents/2124567890-kv-prefetch-delta
maria: leaving this thread but will keep an eye on dashboards. ping me if anything spikes again.
samir: closing incident thread when monitoring stable for 1h. current: eviction rate trending down, batch latency normalizing.
ops-bot: Node maintenance: node-07 marked for deeper investigation (memprofiling). ticket created #INC-8821.
inc_bot: Incident closed (automated) — will reopen if alerts re-trigger in next 60m.
samir: postmortem template: include exact flag diffs, telemetry gaps, improved canary gates.
devon: assigning postmortem to myself, will include timeline, impact, mitigation, and recommended follow-ups.
julie: customer comms sent and acknowledged by 2 customers, one asked for more details on root cause, will coordinate with devon.
samir: thanks team. good catch and quick mitigation. :fire:
